data.reasoning: Both models independently reviewed the PKGBUILD and found it safe. It is a standard binary AUR package that downloads precompiled binaries from the official upstream GitHub repository (akunzai/duodiff) with pinned SHA256 checksums. The package() function only installs the binary to /usr/bin and documentation to standard locations. No injection patterns, no execution of fetched content, no network requests to unrelated hosts, and no .install hooks. data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is artificial - Report 1 (qwen3-235b) returned 'inconclusive' solely because the LLM API request failed with HTTP 400 when auditing .SRCINFO. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all files including .SRCINFO and found it safe. Both models agreed the PKGBUILD itself is safe. This is a tool failure, not a security disagreement.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to audit .SRCINFO due to HTTP 400 API error, resulting in an inconclusive overall verdict despite the file being a plain metadata file with no executable content
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be distinguished from genuine security disagreements when determining if re-audit is needed
For metadata-only files like .SRCINFO, a fallback heuristic could mark them safe without LLM review since they contain no executable code by design
When one report fails due to tool error and another succeeds on the same files, the successful report's verdict should carry full weight rather than triggering an inconclusive escalation
